l4_steps.name: Compute reserve coverage requirements by base
l4_steps.input: Historical sick-call rates, IROPS frequency data, scheduled pairing volume
l4_steps.output: Reserve pool size targets by base, fleet type, and crew position
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve callout success rate ≥95% within 60 min; reserve buffer ≥110% of forecast open duties
l4_steps.pain_point: Historical sick-call rates underestimate demand during seasonal IROPS surges; model recalibration requires manual analyst intervention — no auto-refresh in Jeppesen planning module

l4_steps.name: Allocate reserve positions per CBA obligations
l4_steps.input: Reserve coverage targets, collective bargaining agreement (CBA) reserve-day ratios
l4_steps.output: Reserve allocation roster by base, fleet, and crew position (Captain / FO / FA)
l4_steps.kpi: CBA compliance rate 100%; reserve allocation published ≥72 hours before period start
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA restrictions on reserve obligation days limit scheduling flexibility; union grievances filed when allocation violates contractual reserve windows or exceeds maximum days-on-call

l4_steps.name: Validate reserve pool adequacy vs. coverage model
l4_steps.input: Reserve allocation roster, demand forecast, known vacation/training commitments
l4_steps.output: Approved reserve pool plan or escalation to Director of Crew Scheduling
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve pool adequacy score ≥90% across all bases; gap closure within 48 hours of identification
l4_steps.pain_point: Coverage model accuracy degrades during network-wide weather events; no predictive depletion forecast natively in Jeppesen — requires manual scenario modelling in spreadsheets

l4_steps.name: Detect open crew position from absence or IROPS
l4_steps.input: Real-time crew absence notification (sick call, no-show), flight disruption alert from NOC
l4_steps.output: Open duty record with flight ID, departure time, required crew position, and base
l4_steps.kpi: Open duty detection latency ≤10 min from absence notification; 100% of open duties logged before T-90 min departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Sick-call surges during IROPS overwhelm scheduler capacity; legacy Jeppesen alert queues do not auto-triage by urgency, forcing manual prioritisation under time pressure

l4_steps.name: Query available reserve crew by qualification match
l4_steps.input: Open duty requirements (base, fleet type, position), current reserve availability roster
l4_steps.output: Ranked shortlist of available reserves sorted by CBA callout obligation (earliest callout first)
l4_steps.kpi: Query response time ≤2 min; shortlist generated for 100% of open duties before callout initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen does not automatically apply all CBA tie-breaker rules in the sort order; schedulers manually override, introducing errors and exposing airline to union grievances

l4_steps.name: Initiate automated reserve callout sequence
l4_steps.input: Ranked reserve shortlist, open duty details (flight, departure, report time)
l4_steps.output: Callout attempt log; crew acceptance or declination response captured
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve answer rate ≥85% within 30 min of first callout; callout-to-assignment cycle ≤45 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew unreachable on personal phones during off-duty sleep periods; no regulatory mandate requiring reserve crew to answer within a defined window in all jurisdictions, creating unpredictable response latency

l4_steps.name: Escalate to secondary reserve or open-time board
l4_steps.input: Failed callout log, remaining eligible reserve list, CBA open-time posting rules
l4_steps.output: Secondary callout initiated or duty posted to open-time voluntary pickup board
l4_steps.kpi: Secondary escalation resolution ≤45 min; open-time fill rate ≥70% within 60 min of posting
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve pool exhaustion during cascading IROPS requires manager authorisation to use voluntary overtime; CBA overtime budgets frequently exhausted mid-event, forcing flight cancellations

l4_steps.name: Validate FAR Part 117 rest requirements
l4_steps.input: Reserve crew duty history, callout date/time, proposed report time, cumulative flight duty period
l4_steps.output: Legality check result (legal / illegal); disqualification flag with violation code if illegal
l4_steps.kpi: Legality check completion ≤1 min per crew member; 0 illegal pairings assigned per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Rest period calculations for reserve crews differ from lineholder rules under FAR 117; system may not correctly flag cumulative fatigue across split reserve periods (FAR 117.25), requiring manual secondary checks

l4_steps.name: Verify aircraft type currency and recency
l4_steps.input: Reserve crew qualification record, assigned aircraft type, last operating date, training records feed from LMS
l4_steps.output: Currency and recency confirmation or disqualification flag with expiry date
l4_steps.kpi: Zero misassignment events due to lapsed currency; qualification check latency ≤1 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Currency lapses during extended reserve periods not proactively surfaced; recency tracking in Jeppesen relies on accurate and timely training record feeds from the LMS — data latency causes stale qualification status

l4_steps.name: Confirm route-specific qualifications (ETOPS/special airports)
l4_steps.input: Assigned flight route, special qualification requirements (ETOPS, high-altitude, noise-sensitive airports), crew qualification record
l4_steps.output: Route qualification confirmed or reassignment required with reason code
l4_steps.kpi: Zero ETOPS qualification violations; 100% route compliance rate
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS qualification status not always current in crew tracking system due to training record feed delays; manual cross-check with training department adds 10–15 min to assignment cycle

l4_steps.name: Assign reserve crew to open duty in system
l4_steps.input: Validated crew record, open duty ID, legality and qualification confirmation
l4_steps.output: Confirmed crew assignment; updated roster visible to crew, airport ops, and dispatch
l4_steps.kpi: Assignment completion ≤5 min from legality confirmation; roster visibility propagated to all systems ≤2 min post-assignment
l4_steps.pain_point: Simultaneous assignment attempts by multiple schedulers during IROPS cause optimistic locking conflicts in Jeppesen; failed writes require manual retry, adding delay during time-critical coverage windows

l4_steps.name: Notify reserve crew via mobile push notification
l4_steps.input: Confirmed assignment record (flight, report time, gate, hotel/transport if applicable)
l4_steps.output: Push notification delivered to crew device; crew digital acknowledgment captured
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery ≤2 min of assignment; crew acknowledgment receipt rate ≥92% within 15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Notification failures when crew device is offline or app version is outdated; no guaranteed delivery SLA from mobile OS push services (APNs/FCM) — silent failures require fallback SMS or phone call

l4_steps.name: Brief crew on flight plan, NOTAMs, and special conditions
l4_steps.input: Flight plan package, NOTAM briefing pack, weather advisory, airport operational notices
l4_steps.output: Crew briefed and sign-off recorded; briefing record logged with timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing completion ≥30 min prior to departure for 100% of reserve activations; zero regulatory briefing compliance failures
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew unfamiliar with last-minute route changes or unfamiliar destination airports; time pressure in IROPS degrades briefing thoroughness, increasing risk of operating with incomplete situational awareness

l4_steps.name: Monitor reserve pool utilization in real time
l4_steps.input: Live reserve assignment data, remaining available reserves by base and fleet type
l4_steps.output: Reserve utilization dashboard; automated alert triggered at depletion threshold breach
l4_steps.kpi: Alert triggered when available reserves ≤20% of pool; dashboard refresh interval ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Dashboard refresh latency during high-volume IROPS masks true pool depletion until critically low; Jeppesen base module lacks predictive depletion forecast — operational awareness depends on manual monitoring

l4_steps.name: Post voluntary extension offer to open-time board
l4_steps.system: IBS Software iCrew (open-time posting) + Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: Pool depletion alert, CBA voluntary overtime eligibility rules, remaining open duties
l4_steps.output: Voluntary extension offers posted and crew responses captured; coverage gap delta updated
l4_steps.kpi: Voluntary coverage fill rate ≥70% within 60 min of posting; overtime authorisation cycle ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA limits on forced extensions restrict scheduler options during IROPS; voluntary overtime budget frequently exhausted during prolonged disruptions, leaving residual open duties uncovered

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved open duties to NOC for cancellation decision
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + NOC Operations Board
l4_steps.input: Unresolved open duty list, remaining reserve pool status, downstream flight impact assessment
l4_steps.output: NOC decision: cancel flight, sub-fleet, or continue with substitution plan; cancellation record logged
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation-to-decision cycle ≤30 min; cancellation decision communicated to all stakeholders ≤10 min post-decision
l4_steps.pain_point: NOC cancellation decisions during cascading IROPS require simultaneous crew, aircraft, and gate inputs — single-system views in SITA AMS delay decision quality; lack of integrated crew-aircraft-gate dashboard extends resolution time

l4_steps.name: Update FTL and fatigue counters post-reserve duty
l4_steps.input: Completed duty log, actual block hours, actual duty period start/end times
l4_steps.output: Updated crew flight time limitation (FTL) records, cumulative fatigue counters, rest period start
l4_steps.kpi: FTL record update SLA ≤4 hours post-duty completion; 100% record accuracy verified by audit
l4_steps.pain_point: Late inbound flight data delays FTL record updates; accumulated entry errors trigger false legality alerts in the next scheduling cycle, blocking legal crew assignments and requiring manual override

l4_steps.name: Analyse reserve utilisation metrics for planning feedback
l4_steps.input: Reserve duty assignment history, callout response logs, pool depletion events, IROPS correlation data
l4_steps.output: Monthly reserve utilisation report with callout success trends and pool size recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly report delivered within 5 business days of period close; callout success rate trend ≥95%; report consumed in next planning cycle within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Analytics data latency from Jeppesen to the data warehouse (AWS Redshift) averages 6–12 hours; IROPS events skew utilisation metrics and must be manually isolated from baseline planning to avoid over-provisioning reserve pools
